name: until
algorithm: Split one log file (the generated input, 50 MB of variable-length lines) into records through each standard library's buffered file reader with a 64 KiB buffer and its take-until-delimiter call, once on newline and once on space, r times; prints the records and the bytes taken, each record with its delimiter (Mk fs.File.Reader and Reader.Until, D-331 and D-349; Go bufio.Reader.ReadSlice over os.File; Rust BufReader::read_until over File; Zig std.Io.File.Reader with takeDelimiterInclusive; C has no cell: the Windows UCRT has no getdelim). std-rewrite review RW-9.

skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the counts, which stay below 2^33
skip.c: no take-until-delimiter call in the Windows UCRT (no getdelim), the C library of this table's machine; a per-byte getc loop would be a different algorithm from the other cells' library calls (plan/06-m6.md 4.1; std-rewrite review SRW-RR-5). until.c is the getdelim cell for a C library that has it, not built here

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the record count and the byte total check that every reader split the file the same way
notes: The input is std-regex's (same kind, size and seed), so tools/bench generates it once.
Written by std-rewrite, M6 fix round, 2026-11-08 (review RW-9); checksums from the Go column's run.

SRW-RR-5 (2026-11-08): the C cell is withdrawn. On Windows it ran a hand-written _getc_nolock loop, not a library delimiter call, so it was not the task the other cells measure; section 4.1 gives such a language a cell that says so. Ratios of this row against the fastest peer no longer include C.
